title: Forty years of erosion data, one day of carbon data
subtitle: US cultivated cropland, 2022 NRI release. The erosion panel stopped improving in 1997. The soil-carbon record has one timepoint and therefore no trend at all.

x.label: NRI measurement year
x.note: These nine years are the complete set of national NRI erosion estimates. All nine are taken from the 2022 release, which restates its own history; they must never be mixed with values published in the 2017 release.

y.label: Average annual soil erosion (tons per acre per year)

series.label: Combined (water + wind)
series.marker: filled circle at every measured year

series.label: Sheet and rill (water)
series.marker: filled circle at every measured year

series.label: Wind
series.marker: filled circle at every measured year

annotations.label: 1997-2022: flat
annotations.detail: Combined rate 5.61 -> 5.34 t/ac/yr, -4.8% in 25 years. Water erosion has risen 2.7% since 2007 (2.93 -> 3.01).

annotations.style: vertical rule, distinct from the series; label may sit outside the plot
annotations.label: RaCA, field seasons 2010-11
annotations.detail: The only national measurement of soil organic carbon stocks the United States has ever made. 1,263 cropland sites; one lab-measured pedon each; one timepoint. Never repeated. No rate of change is computable from it.

annotations.label: 2022: 56.5 M acres of cultivated cropland (18.0%) still erode above T, the tolerable-loss rate - 3.6 M acres more than in 2007
The 2022 NRI Summary Report runs to 222 pages and nine measurement years. The word 'carbon' does not appear in it once.

source_note: USDA-NRCS, 2022 National Resources Inventory Summary Report (June 2026; complete 12,666,474-byte direct-from-agency copy, SHA-256 5aa1b976...c58c), Tables 10, 15, 16, 17 and 18. RaCA counts and stock from Soil Survey Staff and T. Loecke, 2016, Rapid Carbon Assessment: Methodology, Sampling, and Summary, S. Wills (ed.), USDA-NRCS, Tables 2 and 8. Erosion values are modelled (USLE / WEQ) estimates at NRI sample points, not field-measured soil loss.
one_claim: The United States measures cropland erosion nine times over forty years and cropland soil carbon once - and the erosion it does measure stopped improving a quarter-century ago.
